column1: # Requirements for the Mica::Deflate, Mica::Zlib and Mica::Gzip encoders
# (milestone Z2, the pure-Crystal Deflate encoder): what RFC 1951 (DEFLATE),
# RFC 1950 (zlib) and RFC 1952 (gzip) require of a compliant compressor, the
# public API, and the size, memory and round-trip properties the encoder
# keeps. zlib 1.2.12 is the reference: every stream Mica writes decodes in it.

column3: Every stream the encoder writes (raw DEFLATE, zlib, gzip; levels 0 to 9; one-shot and streaming) decodes in Mica to the original input
Every stream the encoder writes decodes in system zlib to the original input
An empty input, one byte, a short text, long runs, incompressible bytes, an input longer than the window and a repeat exactly 32,768 bytes back round-trip at every level
A finished stream ends with exactly one block that sets BFINAL, also for an empty input
Level 0 writes only stored blocks of at most 65,535 bytes, and data that does not compress is stored at every level, so the output never grows by more than a few bytes per block
Matches have lengths 3 to 258 and distances 1 to 32,768, and the encoder reaches both maxima
Each block is written as the smallest of stored, fixed Huffman and dynamic Huffman
Dynamic blocks use literal/length and distance codes of at most 15 bits and a code-length code of at most 7 bits, also for heavily skewed frequencies
A zlib stream starts with CM 8, CINFO 7, the FLEVEL zlib writes for the level and a valid FCHECK
With a preset dictionary the header sets FDICT and carries the dictionary's Adler-32, the data refers to the dictionary's last 32 KiB, and the stream decodes only with that dictionary
A zlib stream ends with the Adler-32 of the input, most significant byte first
Without a header a gzip member has no optional fields, MTIME 0, OS 255 and the XFL zlib writes for the level
FTEXT, MTIME, XFL, OS, FEXTRA, FNAME and FCOMMENT of a given header are written and read back unchanged
A file name or comment with a zero byte, or an extra field longer than 65,535 bytes, raises ArgumentError
A gzip member ends with the CRC-32 of the input and its size modulo 2^32, least significant byte first
Levels 0 to 9 are accepted by every encode and writer; any other level raises ArgumentError
The same input, level and options give the same bytes on every call
One write, one-byte writes and writes of random sizes produce streams that decode to the same bytes
After flush the output so far ends on a byte boundary with an empty stored block and decodes to everything written before it; a second flush with nothing written adds no bytes
After full_flush the rest of the stream decodes on its own: no match reaches back past the flush
close finishes the stream once, flushes the destination and closes it only with sync_close
Writing to a closed writer raises IO::Error, and reading from a writer raises IO::Error
At levels 1 to 9 the output is within 1% of system zlib's at the same level on text, binary-like and repetitive samples
A streaming encoder at level 9 holds at most 384 KiB for its window, hash chains and symbol buffer, whatever the input size
Across generated inputs, containers, levels, chunkings and flush points, system zlib and Mica decode every encoded stream to the original
